meters.label: Page reads showing a wrong total

frames.narration: A cart has a subtotal of 100 and a one-time coupon of 10, so the right total is 90. In the first design total() also spends the coupon the first time it runs. The page needs the total in three places.
The first read shows 90 and spends the coupon. The next two show 100. One method, three calls, two different answers: the page disagrees with itself, and 2 of 3 reads show a wrong total.
Someone adds a debug log line that calls total() first. Now the log line gets 90 and the whole page shows 100: all 3 reads are wrong. Looking at the value changed the value.
Separate them. applyCoupon() is a command, called once at checkout. total() is a pure query. Now the page shows 90, 90, 90, with or without the log line, in any order.
Now a ticket counter at 7, with two workers. Applying the rule strictly gives peek() and advance(). Both workers peek 7 before either advances, so both are issued ticket 7.
Both then advance: the counter ends at 9, ticket 8 is lost and ticket 7 was handed out twice. Splitting an indivisible read-then-change created a race that was not there before.

The fix is a deliberate, named exception: takeTicket() reads and changes in one atomic step. One worker gets 7, the other 8, the counter ends at 9. Pop, increment-and-get and compare-and-set are the same kind of method.
The rule is a default, not a law. Keep reads pure so they are safe to repeat, keep changes in visible commands, and allow the few indivisible operations as named exceptions with a comment saying why.
